The Dow Jones Industrial Average on Thursday were slumping, pushing the blue-chip gauge into the red for the year and threatening a second straight decline as consumer-staples shares declined. Most recently, the Dow DJIA, -0.34% was off about 154 points, or 0.6%, at 24,593, with shares of Procter & Gamble Co. PG, -3.27% and Apple Inc. AAPL, -2.83% weighing on the average. For the year, the Dow is off 0.5%, but it is still maintaining a weekly advance of 1%. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 index SPX, -0.57% is up 0.5% for the first four months of the year and 1.1% for the week, so far. The Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, -0.78% was up 4.7% so far in 2018, and up 1.7% for the week thus far. P&G shares were under pressure after the seller of Gillette razors and Crest toothpaste agreed to acquire a consumer-health business from Germany’s Merck KGaA MRK, +0.32%
